$comment: ASSUMED pending owner review — brief-001 D6, distilled from docs/design/data-model.md. The public contract for `retro export --format json`; user-written import scripts read this. Breaking changes = new version (KC-0009: JSON-only export, no tracker integrations). Default export carries ALL decided records with their states; consumers filter (CLI --state approved narrows).
title: retro.export.v1

project.$comment: Nullable since KC-0020: `session create --project` is optional and nothing groups by it. Relaxed additively — every v1 document written before remains valid.

title.$comment: Added by KC-0020: the retrospective's plain-language name, taken from the final revision. Additive — not required, so every v1 document written before remains valid.

finishMessages.$comment: Added by r-finish-confirm-message: the human's final word on each round, written in the confirm step of the Finish button and delivered separately from the comments — a thread is a conversation the AI answers, this is a summary it reads. One entry per revision round he left one on, ascending by `revision`; a round he left none on has no entry, and `[]` is a retrospective he never wrote one for. Human-only — the AI can never write it (architecture.md §Actor model). Additive: not required, so every v1 document written before the field existed remains valid, and a consumer reading one treats an absent key as `[]`.

reviewed.$comment: Constant by construction: only the human can finish a review, only in the UI (data-model.md §Dropped from v2).

reviewThreads.$comment: Review-level threads not anchored to any record.

record.$comment: Final revision's narrative + final human decision fields. Per-record history stays queryable via CLI/UI, never exported (KC-0011).

globalId.$comment: Added by the global record ids change: the record's number across the whole ledger, minted the first time its `rid` appeared in its retrospective and never moved. This is the number the product shows and the one a human cites; `rid` and `num` are both scoped to the retrospective (a rid is minted per retro and repeats across them, and every retro has a record `num` 1), so this is the only key on a record that identifies it on its own. It is stored beside the revision rather than inside it, because a revision is the AI's immutable draft and this is the one name on a record the AI does not author. Additive: not required, so every v1 document written before it stays valid, and a consumer reading one falls back to `(retrospective.id, rid)`.

num.$comment: The record's position **within its own retrospective**, 1-based and dense — minted at first appearance and never renumbered or reused. Still required and still emitted; it stopped being the number the product displays when `globalId` arrived, and stays in the contract because it is real data every document since v1 has carried.

state.$comment: Never `pending`: the finish gate refuses finishing while any record is pending (data-model.md §Retrospective). `revise` is the third verdict (retro 4 r-verdict-revise) and is admitted because the type is `Exclude<DecisionState,'pending'>` and a published contract may not be narrower than the type it serialises; no document written today carries one, because closing a review to export refuses while a record still asks to be rewritten. `hold` is read-only history since retro 3 r-hold-semantics — it left the verdict axis and became `held` below; no new document carries it, and every document written before stays valid.

held.$comment: READ-ONLY HISTORY. Added by r-hold-semantics as the lifecycle flag beside `state`; retro 4 r-remove-hold removed the feature and the builder no longer emits this key. It stays in the contract because this record object is additionalProperties:false, so dropping it would invalidate every document written while the feature existed — the same rule that keeps a `hold` verdict readable. A consumer deciding whether to pick an item up reads `involvement`. It is optional, so a document written after the removal is valid without it.

holdNote.$comment: READ-ONLY HISTORY, as `held` above: why the human parked it, verbatim. Nothing writes this key since retro 4 r-remove-hold.

solutionLevel.$comment: The ceiling the human approved, not a target (v2 solution-levels semantics). On a record carrying `solutions` it is the level of the solution named by `selectedSolution`, not a dial the human turned separately. No longer in `required`, alongside `agreedDirection` and `footprint`: the builder emits one for every record it writes today, and the contract stops insisting so that a future shape which has no single ceiling stays representable without a v2.

workaround.$comment: Free text, or the literal string "none"; never absent.

agreedDirection.$comment: READ-ONLY HISTORY, as `held`/`holdNote` are: the record's one narrative direction, on every record filed before the owner's multi-solution design replaced it with `solutions`. No longer required and no longer emitted; the contract goes on admitting it because this record object is additionalProperties:false, so dropping it would invalidate every document written while it existed — which is all five of the owner's retrospectives. Narrow the write path, never the read path (data-model.md §Hold).

footprint.$comment: READ-ONLY HISTORY, as `agreedDirection` above: the record's one tree of affected files. A record carrying `solutions` has one footprint per solution instead.

solutions.$comment: What the AI proposed, one to three ways, sorted from the lowest level to the highest with exactly one recommended (the owner's multi-solution design). Present on a record filed after that change, in place of `agreedDirection` and `footprint`. Additive: not required, so every document written before it stays valid.

selectedSolution.$comment: A 1-based position into `solutions`, matching the page's "Solution N" titles — the order of that array is the identity of a solution, so 2 means the second element and not an id of any kind, and a 0-based consumer reads the wrong one silently (retro 7, r-export-selected-solution-note). Which solution the human's verdict is for. Present exactly when `solutions` is — it is the human's answer to a question the earlier shape never asked. A reviewer who accepted the AI's recommendation is recorded here as having selected it: the selection carries the recommendation forward rather than being left empty, so a consumer never has to re-derive what was approved.

reviewerNote.$comment: The human's free channel, verbatim. When involvement is `other`, its meaning lives here.

finishMessage.$comment: One round's final message. `revision` is the revision whose round it closes — the same key `ReviewFinished` carries — so a three-round retrospective can carry three of these and a reader can tell which one each belongs to.

component.$comment: Record sections per data-model.md §Comment threads; `review` only inside reviewThreads. `solutions` was added with the owner's multi-solution design; `direction` and `footprint` stay because threads anchored to them exist and human comments are never deleted.

resolved.$comment: Added by r-resolvable-comments: whether the human marked this thread dealt with. Human-only — the AI can never write it (architecture.md §Actor model). Additive: not required, so every v1 document written before the flag existed remains valid, and a consumer reading one treats an absent key as `false`.

revision.$comment: Added by comments_add_revision: the revision this message belongs to. Stored when the writer captured it; otherwise derived from the revision timestamps, which says which revision was current rather than which the writer was reading. Additive: not required, so every v1 document written before the column existed remains valid.
